title: Meta Muse vs Grok Bot vs Instinct for Job Search: Which Agent Applies? (2026)
summary: Meta Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct all promise to act for you. Tsenta compares job search, résumés and applications in 2026, and which can submit for you.
body_markdown:
**No, there is no Instinct connector that applies to jobs for you as of November 20, 2026, and neither Meta nor Grok Bot’s maker names a job-application connector for its agent.** Instinct’s public pages name only one service you can link, Google Workspace, and describe no custom connectors or MCP servers, so even Tsenta, an MCP server that connects to your AI assistant and applies to jobs, has no documented Instinct setup yet. All three agents can work a web browser, so each can attempt an application form you point it to, but none of their makers documents job applications.


Of the three, Grok Bot is the only one whose docs describe adding a remote MCP server by its address, which makes it the likeliest place to connect an applying service such as Tsenta. Meta Muse has the most granular approvals, with up to five choices when it asks, plus a free tier and voice practice that Meta suggests for job interviews. Instinct is the simplest to use: you text or call it, its terms say it is free for now, and if it is at capacity you wait for a welcome text. Muse here means Meta’s personal AI agent, not The Muse job board.


Published November 20, 2026. Tsenta publishes this comparison and sells an agent that applies to jobs. We read each maker’s own pages, help centers and terms that day, but did not run signed-in applications in Muse, Grok Bot or Instinct. We compare what each agent can do for a job seeker, not how well it handles errands or work tasks.


## Meta Muse vs Grok Bot vs Instinct, compared for job search


**Meta Muse** **Grok Bot** **Instinct**


**What it is** Meta’s personal AI agent, with its own cloud computer and browser An AI “teammate” on a cloud computer with a browser, command line and files A personal assistant you text or call


**Where you use it** Muse app on mobile, desktop and the web, or in WhatsApp. US, Canada, Singapore and Australia Desktop app on macOS, Windows and Linux, plus iOS and Android apps Text or call. Sign up with your phone number


**Available connectors** Gmail, Google Calendar, Instagram, Notion, Slack, Box, Dropbox, Canva and more. Full list only in the app. Custom connectors that Muse creates App catalog with Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slack, Notion and Linear. Custom connectors by server URL Google Workspace, for your email inbox and calendar, is the only one its public pages name


**Add a remote MCP server** Not described on Meta’s user pages Yes, as a custom connector or by asking a Bot Not described


**Can it apply to jobs?** No job feature. Its browser can fill out online forms with your approval No job feature. Its browser fills forms and hands you CAPTCHAs, single sign-on and sites that require a human No job feature. It says it can use a computer “in the same way that you do”


**Résumé tailoring** No résumé feature named. Reads, edits and generates documents and PDFs None in the docs. User-shared Bot templates tailor a résumé to one post None described. It keeps files you send it


**Application tracking** No job tracker named. Spaces you describe, recurring tasks, email and Notion connectors None in the docs. Google Sheets and Notion apps, routines and user-shared tracker templates Not documented. Email and calendar through Google Workspace


**Price (as of November 20, 2026)** Free with a weekly usage limit. Power $20 a month, Maximum $100 a month Included with The X Subscription: Premium $30 a month, Super $100, Ultra $200. Plus at $8 excludes it Currently free, per its terms. Paid prices: Not published


**Tsenta’s MCP server** No documented setup yet Possibly, as a custom connector. No Tsenta guide yet No documented setup yet


Prices are each maker’s USD list prices (Grok Bot’s exclude tax), from[Meta’s Muse subscriptions page](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/) ,[Grok Bot’s pricing docs](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/pricing) and[Instinct’s terms](https://instinct.com/terms) . “Not described” and “not documented” mean the maker’s public pages did not mention it on November 20, 2026. Meta says Muse’s full connector list is only in the app’s settings, so a connector can exist there without a public page.


## Can Meta Muse, Grok Bot or Instinct apply to jobs by themselves?


Not as a feature. None of the pages we read from Meta, Grok Bot’s docs or Instinct mentions job applications, résumés or job boards. What each agent has is a browser, and an application is a web form, so each can attempt one when you point it at a posting and give it your details. Here is what stands in the way, from each maker’s own pages:


- **Meta Muse.** Meta’s[browser help](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2124746764949121/) lists “Filling out online forms” among the tasks Muse can do, and Muse asks for approval in line with your settings. Meta’s[security post](https://muse.ai/blog/security-and-safety-for-ai-agents-our-approach-with-muse) says its browser classifiers watch for “attempted submission of high risk forms” and either block the action or ask you to review it. Meta does not say whether a job application counts as one.[Muse’s terms](https://muse.ai/terms) bar circumventing CAPTCHAs or another site’s terms of service.
- **Grok Bot.**[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) list the steps a Bot hands back to you: single sign-on or a passkey, a CAPTCHA it couldn’t get past, an approval on another device or a QR code, a bank card verification and a site that explicitly requires a human.[Its FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq) adds that some sites block traffic from cloud computers.
- **Instinct.** Its[privacy policy](https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) says its browser can act on sites you have not connected.[Its terms](https://instinct.com/terms) say it may make errors, that actions “may not always be reversible” and that “Records of Actions available through Instinct may not always be accurate.”


Muse’s and Instinct’s terms both require you to keep “meaningful human oversight” over what the agent does. So any of the three can try an application, one form at a time, with you nearby for the steps it hands back. Check the employer’s confirmation email for each one rather than the agent’s summary. For how applying agents work and where they stop, see[how AI agents apply to jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-ai-agents-apply-to-jobs-2026) .


## Meta Muse for job search


[Meta launched Muse](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/) on September 8, 2026, as “a personal AI agent” that “can open a browser, fill out forms, and negotiate” for you. Each user gets a[Muse Secure VM](https://muse.ai/) , “a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use.” Meta’s newsroom lists Muse in the US, Canada, Singapore and, since November 17,[Australia](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/muse-is-now-available-in-australia/) . As of November 20, 2026, it is[free with a weekly usage limit](https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/) , with a Power plan at $20 a month for 500M Muse tokens a week and a Maximum plan at $100 a month for 3B. Meta publishes no number for the free allowance.


### Where Muse is strongest


- **Approvals you can tune.** In[Muse’s permissions](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1385290430137537/) , the connector setting “Ask for some actions” asks before every write action and important read actions, and “Always ask” asks before any action. A separate web access setting can ask before Muse opens any website. Approval options can include Allow once, Allow for this task, Allow for this site, Always allow or Deny. Logins go into a[Secure Credentials Store](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2124746764949121/) , so the model does not see your passwords.
- **Interview practice.** Meta’s[voice post](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/introducing-muse-ai-voice-expressive-avatars/) suggests using Muse to “Prepare for a job interview” out loud. It is the only use for job seekers that any of the three makers names.
- **Documents and a tracker you describe.** Muse can[read, edit or generate](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1331373868832401/) PDFs, spreadsheets and documents, so it can draft a résumé version for you to check. A[Space](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/introducing-spaces-customize-muse-app/) is a custom view you describe, such as a tracker, and Muse can[run recurring tasks](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1484325780075655/) daily or weekly.
- **Email.** You can[connect your email, such as Gmail](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1687253048996149/) , and Muse can have[its own email address](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1149305437517250/) . Meta says Muse asks for approval before it sends an email.


### Where Muse falls short for a job search


Meta names no job board, résumé or job-application connector. The[connectors Meta names](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business) are mostly work and shopping tools, such as Asana, Notion, Shopify and Slack. Muse’s[skills](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/2797651547267109/) “are developed by Meta and are already part of Muse,” and Meta describes no way to add a third-party or job-search skill. You can ask Muse to[create a custom connector](https://www.meta.com/help/superintelligence/1687253048996149/) , which “can involve retrieving API information from the service,” and Meta says it does not review custom connectors. Our guide to[applying to jobs with Meta Muse](https://tsenta.com/blog/meta-muse-apply-to-jobs-2026) walks through a reviewed workflow.


### Meta Muse connector: can Tsenta add applying?


Not as a documented setup yet. Meta says Muse can write its own custom connectors for other services, but its public Muse pages do not describe adding a remote MCP server by its address. Meta’s[connector platform](https://platform.muse.ai/docs) asks businesses for their API or MCP documentation and reviews each connector before it appears in Muse, which is a route for companies rather than for you. If your Muse account supports custom remote MCP servers, give it Tsenta’s server address,` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` , and sign in with OAuth.


Because Muse is an agent that can browse and act on websites, it can open tsenta.com and work in your Tsenta account in its browser, the way you would. That is ordinary browsing, not a Muse connector or integration.


## Grok Bot for job search


[Grok Bot](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview) calls itself “your proactive AI teammate”: an agent with a persistent cloud computer that has a browser, command line and files, and keeps working while your laptop is closed.[Grok Bot 1.0](https://x.ai/news/grok-bot-1-0) launched on November 11, 2026, after a beta. It runs in a desktop app on macOS, Windows and Linux and a companion app on iOS and Android, according to[its FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq) . As of November 20, 2026, it is[included](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/pricing) with The X Subscription’s Premium plan at $30 a month, Super at $100 and Ultra at $200, with usage drawn from a weekly pool shared with Grok and Cursor. Plus, at $8 a month, does not include it, and some accounts can try it first with a usage credit that has a 7-day window.


### Where Grok Bot is strongest


- **The only one of the three that lets you add a remote MCP server yourself.** Its overview says “Grok Bot supports custom tooling, so it can interact with any MCP or API,” and its[apps docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) describe adding one by server URL. A job-search or applying service can plug in without the maker’s involvement.
- **Scheduled work.** A[skill saves how to do a task and a routine](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/skills-routines-and-automations) runs a workflow on a schedule, so a Bot can run a daily search and send you a shortlist.
- **Spreadsheets and notes.** Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Notion apps let a Bot keep a tracker in a sheet. The docs say apps “are more reliable than clicking through a website when one exists.”
- **Its own inbox.** You can claim an address at mail.grokbot.com for your Bots, and a Bot can read one-time codes from a connected Gmail or Outlook account or from that inbox.
- **Approval cards.**[Auto Review](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/approvals-security-and-privacy) checks each action and shows an approval card when one needs your OK.


### Where Grok Bot falls short for a job search


The[x.ai marketplace](https://x.ai/bot/marketplace) lists no Bot for job seekers. Its job-related Bots, such as Recruiting Coordinator and Talent Discovery, serve recruiters. Job-search Bots exist as user-shared templates on x.ai links, and each template page says the Bot “was created by a third-party user, not by SpaceXSI,” the company name on x.ai’s pages. Every Bot on your account shares one cloud computer, including its signed-in sessions, files and credentials. At $30 a month, it is also the most expensive of the three to start. Our roundup of[Grok Bot plugins for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-grok-bot-plugins-job-search-2026) reviews the plugins and Bot templates we found. The plugins it covers say they do not submit applications, and the few user-shared templates that say they apply show no proof of submitted applications on their pages.


### Grok Bot plugin: can Tsenta add applying?


Possibly.[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) say that in the desktop app you can open **Connect apps** , choose **Add a custom connector** , enter a name, pick **Remote HTTPS** with a server address and save it with **Add plugin** , or ask a Bot to add an MCP server by its address. Use Tsenta’s server address,` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` , and sign in to Tsenta if asked. Tsenta does not publish a Grok Bot guide yet and is not listed in Grok Bot’s marketplace or app catalog, so check the tools Grok Bot lists after you connect. A connected app is available to every Bot you run, and on a team, an admin’s MCP policy can block saving the server.


## Instinct for job search


[Instinct](https://instinct.com/) is “a personal assistant that understands what you’re working on and what’s important to you,” made by Spear Street Technology. Its homepage says “there are no new interfaces. You can text or call it. It can use a phone and computer in the same way that you do.” Its examples are errands: ordering groceries, booking a train, sending flowers. You sign up with your phone number, and if Instinct is at capacity, its[SMS terms](https://instinct.com/legal/sms-terms.html) say you get a welcome text when your spot opens.[Its terms](https://instinct.com/terms) say Instinct “is currently available without charge,” with notice before any fees, and it has no pricing page.


### Where Instinct is strongest


- **Nothing new to learn.** Its terms say you can message it through a third-party messaging service “without needing to download a separate app.”
- **Free for now.** It is the only one of the three with no paid plan today.
- **Email and calendar.** Linking Google Workspace gives it “your calendar and email inbox,” per its[privacy policy](https://instinct.com/privacy-policy) , which covers recruiter replies and interview scheduling. Instinct says it does not use Google Workspace data to train AI models.
- **It follows up first.** Its terms say Instinct may “proactively send you messages, and provide updates about the tasks you ask Instinct to perform.”


### Where Instinct falls short for a job search


Instinct’s public pages name no connection beyond Google Workspace and have no docs or help pages. They describe no custom connectors or MCP servers, and no job, résumé or tracker feature. Its terms say records of its actions may not be accurate, which matters if you want a reliable log of where you applied. They also make you “solely responsible for ensuring that any Actions Instinct takes on any Third Party Service are permitted” under that service’s terms.


### Instinct connector: can Tsenta add applying?


Not as a documented setup yet. Instinct’s public site does not describe custom connectors or MCP servers, and Tsenta has no Instinct guide. If your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers, add Tsenta’s server address,` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` , and sign in with OAuth. Our guide to[Instinct connectors for job search](https://tsenta.com/blog/instinct-ai-connectors-job-search-2026) covers what Instinct can do in a job search today.


## What Tsenta adds if your agent can connect it


Tsenta is an MCP server that connects to your AI assistant and your own Tsenta account. Tsenta watches 300,000+ company career pages. Once an assistant can reach the server, it gets tools for the steps these three agents leave to you:


- **Find.** Roles ranked against your profile, with filters for keywords, location, remote or hybrid work, pay, experience and date posted. It can read full job descriptions and job links you paste.
- **Tailor.** A résumé tailored for each role in Honest mode, which rewords your existing experience, or Aggressive mode, which rewrites more freely and may stretch claims, or your résumé sent as written. Tsenta drafts a cover letter when the form takes one. Our guide to[connectors that tailor your résumé](https://tsenta.com/blog/ai-assistant-connectors-tailor-resume-2026) compares the options per assistant.
- **Apply.** Applications that Tsenta submits in the cloud on supported company career sites. Only submitted applications count against your allowance.
- **Track.** The status of every application Tsenta starts, a tracker with Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected and Ghosted stages for roles you applied to anywhere, and recruiter emails in your Tsenta inbox. Our[application tracking guide](https://tsenta.com/blog/track-job-applications-ai-assistants-2026) shows the do-it-yourself version for each assistant.


With résumé auto-approval off, each tailored résumé waits for your approval, and form review stops before the final submit on employer systems that support pausing. Your assistant gives those approvals through Tsenta’s tools, so tell it to show you each résumé and form first. One approval gives the assistant every available Tsenta tool on your account, including tools that change account data, and whether it asks before each action depends on the assistant, not on Tsenta. On Starter and Pro you choose each role and Tsenta submits it. Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles within your filters without per-role approval, needs Tsenta’s Power plan.


Your first 25 applications are free, with no card. USD global pricing per 30-day cycle is Starter at $19 a month for 600 applications, Pro at $39 for 1,500 and Power at $99 for 4,500, and connecting an assistant costs nothing extra. See[pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) for quarterly billing and other markets.


Tsenta publishes step-by-step setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex at[tsenta.com/mcp](https://tsenta.com/mcp) . For applying from an assistant with documented steps today, the[Claude connector](https://tsenta.com/connectors/claude) works on every Claude plan, and[Free allows one custom connector](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp) . In ChatGPT, applying needs full MCP support, which[OpenAI lists on Business, Enterprise and Edu](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt) . The[help article](https://help.tsenta.com/connect-claude-chatgpt-mcp) covers privacy, disconnecting and troubleshooting, and our[Claude connectors roundup](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-claude-connectors-job-search-2026) compares the alternatives.


Where the three agents win: Tsenta only handles the job search. Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct also book, buy, schedule and message for you, and Muse can rehearse an interview with you out loud. Tsenta’s networking tools save outreach drafts and never send them, and Tsenta submits on supported company career sites, not on every site.


## Which agent fits your job search


- **You want an agent you can extend:** Grok Bot. It is the only one of the three whose docs describe adding a remote MCP server yourself, by its address, and its routines can run a daily search. It is also the most expensive to start, at $30 a month.
- **You want careful approvals and interview practice:** Meta Muse. It has a free tier, Meta’s $20 Power plan and per-action approvals, and Meta suggests its voice mode for interview practice.
- **You want an assistant you just text or call:** Instinct, for recruiter email and interview scheduling through Google Workspace, while it is free.
- **You want applications sent:** connect an MCP server that applies to an assistant with documented setup, such as Claude, and keep your personal agent for the errands around the search. Our[MCP server comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-mcp-servers-job-search-2026) lists the servers that submit, and our guide to[connecting a job search agent to Claude or ChatGPT](https://tsenta.com/blog/connect-ai-job-search-agent-to-claude-chatgpt-2026) walks through setup.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is there an Instinct connector that applies to jobs for me?


No, there is no Instinct connector that applies to jobs for you as of November 20, 2026. Instinct’s public pages name only Google Workspace, with products such as your email inbox and calendar, as a service you link, and they describe no job connectors, custom connectors or MCP servers. Its browser may attempt a web form, but Instinct does not claim job applications. Tsenta, an MCP server that submits applications on supported company career sites, has no documented Instinct setup yet: if your Instinct account supports custom remote MCP servers, add Tsenta’s server address,[https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp](https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp) , and sign in with OAuth.


### Is there a Muse connector that applies to jobs for me?


No, Meta names no Muse connector that applies to jobs as of November 20, 2026, and Meta’s public Muse pages do not mention job applications, résumés or job boards. Muse’s browser can fill out online forms with your approval, so it can attempt an application one form at a time. Tsenta, an MCP server that submits applications on supported company career sites, has no documented Meta Muse setup yet, because Meta’s public Muse pages do not describe adding a remote MCP server by its address. Meta says Muse can write its own custom connectors for other services, so if your Muse account supports custom remote MCP servers, give it Tsenta’s server address,[https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp](https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp) , and sign in with OAuth.


### Is there a Grok Bot plugin that applies to jobs for me?


Not from Grok Bot’s maker, and no Grok Bot plugin we found applies to jobs for you. The x.ai marketplace lists no Bot for job seekers, and the user-shared Bot templates we found that say they apply show no proof of submitted applications on their pages. Tsenta’s MCP server, which submits applications on supported company career sites, possibly works as a Grok Bot plugin, because Grok Bot’s documentation says it can add a remote MCP server by its address, but Tsenta does not publish a Grok Bot guide yet. In the Grok Bot desktop app, open Connect apps, choose Add a custom connector, enter a name, pick Remote HTTPS, paste[https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp](https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp) and choose Add plugin, then sign in to Tsenta if asked.


### Which is better for job search: Meta Muse, Grok Bot or Instinct?


Grok Bot is the best fit of the three if you want to add job-search tools, Meta Muse if you want fine-grained approvals and interview practice, and Instinct if you want to text an assistant for free. Grok Bot is the only one whose docs describe adding a remote MCP server yourself, and it runs scheduled routines with Google Sheets and Notion. Muse has a free tier, Meta’s Power plan at $20 a month and voice practice Meta suggests for job interviews. None of the three makers documents job applications.


### Can Meta Muse, Grok Bot or Instinct apply to jobs on their own?


They can attempt an application form, but none of the three makers documents job applications as a feature. All three run a web browser: Meta lists filling out online forms as a Muse browser task, Grok Bot hands you single sign-on, passkeys, CAPTCHAs it can’t get past and sites that require a human, and Instinct says it can use a computer the same way you do. Muse’s and Instinct’s terms make you keep meaningful human oversight of what the agent does, so check every application it says it sent.


### How much do Meta Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct cost?


As of November 20, 2026, Meta Muse is free with a weekly usage limit, with Power at $20 a month and Maximum at $100 a month. Grok Bot comes with The X Subscription’s Premium plan at $30 a month, Super at $100 and Ultra at $200, and the $8 Plus plan does not include it. Instinct’s terms say it is currently free, and it publishes no paid prices. Tsenta’s first 25 applications are free with no card, and its USD global plans start at $19 a month for 600 applications.


### Is Meta Muse the same as The Muse job board?


No. Meta Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent, launched on September 8, 2026, at muse.ai. The Muse at themuse.com is a separate job board, and this comparison covers only Meta’s agent.
